To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microtiter plate assay for integrase activity using an immobilized donor DNA substrate can be modified to study the dynamics of enzyme assembly and that the enzyme is multimeric and can exchange subunits during the assembly reaction.

the strand transfer reaction catalyzed by HIV-1 integrase requires the enzyme to bind to a donor substrate in the form of a multimer, that the donor substrate promotes the assembly of the multimer, that this assembly reaction requires MnCl2, and that the multimer is stable in the absence of donor DNA but can be disrupted by the presence of excess MnCl2.

the assembly of the catalytically active human immunodeficiency type 1 integraseme complex on immobilized donor DNA requires high concentrations of divalant cation, that the complex is retained on the donor and is sufficient to catalyse strand transfer with target substrates added subsequently and that the multimerization and self-assembly of the enzyme is promoted by prior incubation in 25 mM manganese chloride.

the development of a microtiter assay to study the biochemical reactions of human immunodeficieny virus type 1 (HIV-1) integrase, the viral enzyme responsible for integrating a DNA copy of HIV into the genome of its host cell.
